body.statement: Using \(\mathsf{FrontierHandle}\), determine an explicit formula or finite structural recurrence solely in \(n,k\) for \(D_k(n)\) at every admissible pair. Prove a universal upper bound equal to that recurrence, construct a graph-query family in \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) attaining it for every pair, and prove that one original directed coefficient separates the retained generic branches. The recurrence must account for forced covariance relations, losses under the exact \(S_G\)-localization and affine dehomogenization, and roots at projective infinity, and must agree with the separately verified values in \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) at \(k=0\) and with \(2^{k+1}\) when \(n\ge2k+4\).
body.justification: The all-size exact frontier, rather than another isolated higher-degree graph, is the theorem-level kernel.
body.gap: The tree papers settle only \(k=0\), while Foygel, Draisma, and Drton compute small whole-fiber degrees; no source gives the maximum single-coordinate degree as a function of both size and excess-parent budget.
body.consumer: The result supplies fasttreeid with an exact ambiguity budget and a sharp stop rule for every supported graph size.
